rounds.text: Arrow Greentech Ltd is significantly under-appreciated, trading at a P/E of 17.35x [E6] and an EV/EBITDA of 10.62x [E11], both of which sit comfortably below their respective sector benchmarks of 23.66x [E6] and 14.55x [E11]. This discount is unjustified given the company's exceptional profitability, boasting an ROE of 22.4% [E13] and an ROCE of 30.4% [E12], which vastly outperform the sector benchmarks of 10.54% [E9] and 12.62% [E10]. Furthermore, the business has demonstrated powerful, fundamentals-led growth with a 5-year compounded profit growth of 51% [E19, E57] and a 3-year compounded sales growth of 23% [E16], supported by a strong macro tailwind in the Capital Goods sector [E72, E74]. Financially, the company is exceptionally robust and virtually debt-free with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.01x [E38, E60] and a comfortable current ratio of 10.33x [E39], while generating Rs 39 Cr in free cash flow as of March 2026 [E36]. A discounted cash flow analysis highlights this deep value, indicating an intrinsic value of Rs 1728 per share against a market price of Rs 771 [E46], representing a 55.4% margin of safety [E47]. Conceded: the company's working capital days have increased from 142 days to 239 days [E65], and its historical peak-to-trough drawdown reached -95.7% [E54].

Despite headline valuation multiples appearing moderate, Arrow Greentech Ltd carries severe structural risks highlighted by a dramatic ballooning of working capital days from 142 to 239 days [E65]. This severe friction in operating efficiency coincides with an inconsistent yearly and quarterly operating-margin trend over the last two years and two quarters respectively [E32, E33], alongside a historical peak-to-trough drawdown of a staggering -95.7% [E54]. Furthermore, the company exhibits extreme annualised volatility of 68.3% [E55], reflecting a history of erratic price behaviour that demands intense caution. Promoter holding has also experienced a contraction from 68.60% in September 2023 down to 65.65% by June 2026 [E42], while short-term borrowings ticked up from Rs 1 Cr to Rs 2 Cr [E40] and capital work-in-progress completely evaporated to zero with a -100% move [E41]. Conceded: the business demonstrates high profitability metrics such as a 30.4% ROCE [E12] and a 22.4% ROE [E13], alongside positive institutional money flow (+0.31 percentage points) [E45]. However, recent price growth exceeding profit growth by 16% signals that expectations are rapidly running ahead of actual delivery [E58], leaving the stock vulnerable to sharp mean reversion given its extreme volatility [E55] and stretched working capital [E65].

The bear highlights ballooning working capital days [E65], but this friction is overwhelmingly offset by a powerful and pristine balance sheet carrying virtually zero debt [E60] and a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.01x [E38]. Conceded: annual and quarterly operating margins show inconsistent trends [E32, E33], yet profitability remains elite with a stellar 30.4% ROCE [E12] and a 22.4% ROE [E13] that completely dwarf sector benchmarks [E10, E9]. While the bear points to historical drawdowns and volatility [E54, E55], the business generated a massive ₹43 Cr in operating cash flow and ₹39 Cr in free cash flow in March 2026 [E35, E36], underpinned by strong sector tailwinds in Capital Goods with a tailwind score of +0.67 [E74]. The minor drop in promoter stake [E42] is entirely neutralized by positive institutional money flow [E45], and rather than expectations running ahead of delivery [E58], the fundamentals-led setup shows 5-year profit growth of 51% vastly outpacing 5-year price growth of 41% [E23, E57].

Conceded: operating cash flow reached Rs 43 Cr and free cash flow hit Rs 39 Cr in March 2026 [E35, E36], alongside a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.01x [E38]. However, the bull's dismissal of ballooning working capital days ignores that they have expanded severely from 142 days to 239 days [E65], signaling a massive operational drain that even a pristine balance sheet does not cure. While the bull points to elite ROCE and ROE [E12, E13], it glosses over the fact that operating-margin trends are explicitly recorded as inconsistent on both yearly and quarterly bases [E32, E33]. Furthermore, the claim that 5-year profit growth outpaces 5-year price growth [E57] conflicts directly with the record showing that price growth recently exceeds profit growth by 16%, proving that market expectations are indeed running ahead of delivery [E58]. Finally, the assertion that the promoter stake drop is neutralized [E42, E45] ignores the direct insider reduction from 68.60% to 65.65% [E42], which occurs alongside extreme annualised volatility of 68.3% [E55] and a devastating historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -95.7% [E54].

Conceded: working capital days have indeed expanded from 142 days to 239 days [E65]. However, the bear's focus on this single metric ignores that the company generated robust operating cash flow of Rs 43 Cr and free cash flow of Rs 39 Cr in March 2026, with cash conversion at a healthy 0.91x [E34, E35, E36]. While the bear highlights inconsistent operating margins [E32, E33], it glosses over the concrete expansion in TTM operating margin to 35% and a quarterly jump to 41% in June 2026 [E30, E31]. The conflict regarding growth pacing is resolved by the 5-year data showing fundamental profit growth at 51% outpacing 5-year price growth at 41% [E57]. Regarding the insider stake drop [E42], the broader institutional picture reveals positive money flow with domestic holdings increasing significantly, alongside a stellar 93/100 rules-based screen score backed by elite returns on capital [E10, E44, E45, E66].

Conceded: operating cash flow reached Rs 43 Cr and free cash flow hit Rs 39 Cr in March 2026 [E35, E36]. However, the bull's dismissal of the ballooning working capital ignores a severe deterioration from 142 days to 239 days [E65], which directly threatens future cash generation. The bull points to TTM and quarterly margin expansions, yet overlooks the official classification of the yearly and quarterly operating-margin trends as inconsistent over the last two periods [E30, E31, E32, E33]. While the bull asserts that 5-year profit growth of 51% outpaces price growth [E57], more recent dynamics show price growth exceeding profit growth by 16%, signalling that market expectations are running dangerously ahead of actual delivery [E58]. Finally, the claim of robust institutional backing glosses over the concrete reduction in promoter holdings from 68.60% to 65.65% [E42], alongside extreme volatility of 68.3% and a catastrophic historical drawdown of -95.7% [E54, E55].
